C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY.Summary: RM-GOVERNED-PATH Phase P0 (steps 4, 6, 10) plus D8.8: cursor and ledger honesty — refuse non-numeric epoch bounds, recover corrupt loose ledgers without deleting run/, surface fail→pass attempt pairs whose non-test ObservedWriteScope digests do not move, and make status distinguish folded from open epochs. Calibration backfill (P0.8) is a separate bundle (D8.1).
C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY.Problem:
The product thesis is that the agent cannot lie to the model. Three live defects invert that for the run ledger and its reports, all verified during P0's own execution of C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY.
P0.4 / F8. Cursor advance --open-epoch accepts --from T-001 / --to T-001: Number("T-001") is NaN, the CLI exits 0, and disk holds run/NaN-T-001-opened.xml with Allocation from="NaN" to="NaN". The same path also accepts 0, negatives, floats, and from > to. Two silent readers then hide the damage (F8.2): EVENT_FILENAME at grace-cursor.ts:437 drops names that fail ^(\d+) at :459 (the live NaN-* file never reaches the id guard), and the integer/positive id guard at :470 drops well-named files whose XML id is not a positive integer. Lint stays green; fold dead-ends with "no Allocation found" once work events exist beside the orphan.
P0.6 / F8.1. There is no cursor recover command and no auto-open for single-controller loose runs. The corpus remedy is rm -r run/ — deleting the audit trail to satisfy the audit gate. The real corrupt ledger (C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY/run/NaN-T-001-opened.xml, Allocation worker="w0" from="NaN" to="NaN") is preserved as the acceptance fixture: the NaN orphan has no recoverable id (D8.3), so nothing can extend an allocation to cover it.
P0.10 / F9 / F9.3. Every cursor attempt already digests WriteEvidence. On C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY, recorded fail→pass pairs for T-001 and T-002 have byte-identical implementation files; T-005's honest pair changed only a test file and is structurally indistinguishable. Red-first is prose in ngrace-execute that nothing reads back. The rule is detection, not prevention: raise a finding the reviewer clears with a recorded reason; do not fail the bundle (F9.3 weakens F9.2).
D8.8 / F8.2. status's epochs field counts folded Epoch-N wrappers only (countLedgerEpochs, grace-status.ts:211), so it reports 0 (or omits) throughout every in-progress open epoch. That misreport made F8 hard to see; it ships here, not deferred (D8.8 overrules the derivation's P3 deferral).
Sequencing (plan.md §1 rule 7): C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY must not archive until this work lands — its ledger carries the corrupt epoch (F8.1) and its attempt records cannot substantiate red-first (F9 / F9.3).
F10 / P0.10 pre-condition. Emitting a new review.* finding code at HEAD trips T-005's catalog completeness test, which demands an exact *lint* guide for a *review* code. Two defects: (1) namespace — review.* is routed to getExactLintIssueGuide instead of REVIEW_CATALOG; (2) blind spot — makeFinding(code, …) is positional and invisible to the scanner, so all 13 existing review codes have zero coverage. The only repair site for the test is src/lint/catalog.test.ts, inside C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY's ObservedWriteScope. F10.2: this bundle declares a sequential overlap on that file and repairs both defects so AC-ATTEMPT-PAIR-FINDING is satisfiable.

Goals.Goal: Validate --from / --to (and library openEpoch bounds) as positive integers with from ≤ to before any write; refuse task ids and the wider invalid matrix; error text names the accepted form and that task ids are not event ids (P0.4).

Surface both silent-skip classes for orphan discovery without widening listLooseEvents' ordered-valid contract (D8.7): filename-regex misses (EVENT_FILENAME :437 / :459) and non-positive / non-integer XML ids (:470).

Auto-open a covering opened/Allocation for single-controller loose runs (one distinct worker value in the ledger∪loose inventory — D8.2); refuse when more than one distinct worker appears and demand an explicit epoch.

cursor recover --change C-ID diagnoses loose events, unterminated ranges, out-of-allocation events, and unrecoverable orphans; --fix extend-allocation writes a recorded covering allocation for valid integer ids, leaves unrecoverable orphans on disk, and makes fold succeed for the valid stream (P0.6 / D8.3). Deleting run/ stops being the documented recovery.

Repair the catalog completeness scanner so review.* and gate.* codes are routed to their own catalogs (never getExactLintIssueGuide), and so makeFinding's positional code argument is visible to the scanner (F10); then ngrace review raises a warning-severity finding when a fail→pass attempt pair on the same task has no non-test ObservedWriteScope file with a differing digest; the reviewer clears it with a recorded reason (F9.3 / D8.6). cursor attempt stays quiet at write time.
status reports distinguish folded epoch count from open (unfolded) epochs so an in-progress run is not labelled epochs=0 (D8.8).

Constraints.Constraint: Binding decisions: D8.1 (P0.8 out of this bundle), D8.2 (worker condition = more than one distinct worker value), D8.3 (NaN orphan stays), D8.6 (clearance is a recorded reason, not a cleared flag), D8.7 (orphan reader parallel to listLooseEvents), D8.8 (status epochs in scope), F8 / F8.1 / F8.2 / F9 / F9.3 / F10 / F10.2.

A29.2 / F1 — the binary writes only structural state it can derive or is explicitly given, never authored content, and never without an explicit apply. Cursor advance / attempt already write on command invocation (regenerate is the dry-run/--apply cousin). Auto-open and recover --fix extend-allocation sit on the permitted side: allocation bounds are derived from the integer loose-event inventory; the operator act is the write command or explicit --fix. Forbidden: inventing an id for a NaN orphan, fabricating multi-worker partitions, rewriting attempt outcomes, deleting run/ events, or hand-editing Allocation attributes.

File-disjoint from active C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY ObservedWriteScope except the single sequential overlap authorized by F10.2: this bundle's write scope includes src/lint/catalog.test.ts so the completeness scanner can be repaired. That path is also listed in C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY's ObservedWriteScope; the overlap is safe because all five of that bundle's tasks are complete (nothing writes those files under that bundle again), no cross-bundle ObservedWriteScope check exists in the tool, and disjointness was an authority discipline being explicitly and narrowly relaxed — not missed. Still out of this bundle: src/lint/catalog.ts, src/project-utils.ts, src/artifact/projections.ts, src/artifact/grammar.ts and their other tests, and C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY's plan/spec and plan.md. recover and bounds validation raise GraceCommandError (or equivalent command errors), not new src/lint/catalog.ts codes. New review.* codes belong in REVIEW_CATALOG (src/review/catalog.ts), not the lint catalog.

Do not edit or --fix the live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY ledger as part of implementing this bundle. That ledger is evidence and the P0.6 acceptance fixture (F8.1). Tests exercise a copy of the corrupt shape. Applying recover --fix to the real C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY run/ is a separate authorized act by the authority before that bundle archives — not an implementation task of this change.

F9.3 — do not re-strengthen the attempt-pair check into an error that fails the bundle or refuses cursor attempt. T-005's honest test-only pair is structurally identical to T-002's suspect pair; a digest cannot read a claim. Detection, not prevention (R3 / F2 ceiling).

Do not set status="approved" in this authoring pass; approval is a human act. This deliverable is spec.xml only (F4 two-stage authoring); plan.xml is a later task after approval. Do not hand-edit CHANGELOG.md (D5.5).
Evidence doctrine: TraceAssertion + tests default; Marker only for runtime trajectory. Write each regression test first, watch it fail on pre-fix code, then fix.

NonGoals.NonGoal: P0.8 calibration backfill / command-run evidence adjudication, any edit under src/calibration/, or fold-time CalibrationAdjudication redesign (D8.1; separate bundle; bound by D6 / corr 156).

Any file in C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY's ObservedWriteScope except the F10.2 carve-out src/lint/catalog.test.ts: src/project-utils.ts|.test.ts, src/artifact/projections.ts|.test.ts, src/artifact/grammar.ts|.test.ts, src/lint/catalog.ts (production catalog — not the completeness test), that bundle's plan/spec, docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/plan.md.

Mass-authoring exact REVIEW_CATALOG guides for every pre-existing review.* code the makeFinding scanner will newly surface (F10). Those land on a frozen commented allowlist and are reported to the authority, same treatment as T-005's lint backlog — not scoped as guide-authoring work here.
Deleting, renaming, or hand-editing C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY/run/NaN-T-001-opened.xml or any event under that bundle's run/ as part of this change.
Relabelling historical fail→pass attempt digests on C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY (F9.1 forbids staged reds); inventing a new finding-clearance ledger schema without an authority decision (D8.6).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EPOCH-BOUNDS-REJECT: cursor advance --open-epoch with --from / --to set to a task id (T-001), a non-integer string, a float (1.5), zero, a negative, or from > to exits non-zero, writes no run/* file, and the error message names positive integer event ids as the accepted form and states that task ids are not event ids. Valid --from 1 --to 10 still opens. advanceCursor({ openEpoch, from, to }) refuses the same invalid matrix at the library boundary, not only the CLI.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ORPHAN-BOTH-SKIPS: A parallel orphan inventory (D8.7) reports both silent-skip classes without changing listLooseEvents' ordered positive-integer contract: (1) run/* names that fail EVENT_FILENAME (grace-cursor.ts:437), including the live NaN-T-001-opened.xml shape dropped at :459; (2) files whose name matches EVENT_FILENAME but whose XML id fails the integer/positive guard at :470. A criterion or fix that only addresses :470 leaves the live F8 defect in place and fails this AC.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECOVER-DIAGNOSE: cursor recover --change C-ID on a copy of the F8.1 shape (NaN-* opened with Allocation from="NaN" to="NaN", plus valid loose integer events, no valid allocation) reports: unrecoverable orphan (no recoverable event id), missing valid covering allocation, the integer loose-event range, and that fold is blocked. No recover subcommand absence remains.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECOVER-FIX-PRESERVES-ORPHAN: On that same copy, recover --fix extend-allocation (or create-covering under the same flag) writes a recorded, ledger-visible opened/Allocation spanning the valid integer loose ids; subsequent fold succeeds for that valid stream. After --fix: the NaN-* orphan file still exists on disk, recover still reports it as an unrecoverable orphan, and no implementation path deletes run/ or the orphan to make fold succeed. A test that only asserts "fold succeeds" without asserting the orphan's continued presence and continued diagnosis does not satisfy this criterion — deletion would pass that weaker bar and is the folklore this step retires (D8.3 / F8.1).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-AUTO-OPEN-SINGLE-CONTROLLER: With loose integer events, no valid open allocation, and at most one distinct worker value in ledger∪loose Allocations (including default w0, and including a single non-default worker such as only-w3 — D8.2), fold or the designated auto-open surface synthesizes a retroactive covering opened spanning those ids. When more than one distinct worker value appears, auto-open refuses and demands an explicit epoch open; multi-worker ranges are never silently fabricated.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-PAIR-FINDING: Depends on AC-REVIEW-CATALOG-NAMESPACE: at HEAD, emitting a new review.* code trips the lint-catalog completeness test (F10); this criterion is unsatisfiable until that repair lands. After the namespace repair: for a fail→pass attempt pair on the same task, when no non-test file in ObservedWriteScope differs in WriteEvidence digest between the two events, ngrace review --change C-ID emits a warning-severity ReviewFinding (illustrative code review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated) registered in REVIEW_CATALOG — not in the lint catalog — that does not fail the bundle. Non-test means paths not ending in .test.ts or .test.js, intersected with the plan's ObservedWriteScope. Corpus shapes: C-TOKEN T-001 events 2→3 and T-002 events 6→7 raise the finding; T-005 events 16→17 (test-only digest change) also raise it (F9.3 — honest case still costs a recorded sentence). cursor attempt does not refuse or warn at write time when digests match. Do not re-strengthen past F9.3 into an error or write-time refusal.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-CATALOG-NAMESPACE: Catalog completeness (src/lint/catalog.test.ts) routes review.* codes to REVIEW_CATALOG and gate.* codes to the gate catalog — never to getExactLintIssueGuide. The completeness scanner recognizes makeFinding's positional code argument (review/core.ts makeFinding(code, file, message, …)), so the thirteen existing review codes become visible to the check rather than invisible to it. Both defects must be fixed; a criterion or change that only re-routes namespaces without teaching makeFinding leaves the blind spot in place, and the reverse leaves the namespace error. Expect the makeFinding repair to surface a backlog of pre-existing review codes without exact REVIEW_CATALOG guides — treat exactly as T-005 treated the lint backlog: a frozen, commented allowlist, reported to the authority, not mass-authored. Regression of the F10 probe: emitting a new review.* code (e.g. review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated via makeFinding or an equivalent object form) must not require a src/lint/catalog.ts entry; bun test src/lint/catalog.test.ts stays green without one.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-PAIR-REASON-RECORDED: Clearing the attempt-pair finding requires a recorded free-text reason, not a boolean "reviewed" flag (D8.6). Until a finding-level ledger schema exists, the reason is recorded on ngrace gate verdict --note keyed by the finding's stable findingId (see Assumptions). A clearance path that records only that the finding was dismissed, without the reviewer's reason text, fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-STATUS-EPOCHS-OPEN-VS-FOLDED: ngrace status distinguishes folded epoch count from open (unfolded) epochs for an active change with an in-progress open epoch and no folded Epoch-N yet: the report does not present a bare epochs=0 (or equivalent) as if no epoch activity exists while run.xml / cursor show report an open epoch. After fold, folded count reflects Epoch-N wrappers. Discriminating negative: a healthy open epoch (from=1 to=N, progress recorded) must not be indistinguishable in the epochs field from a change with no cursor activity at all.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REGRESSION-AND-SUITE: Every conversion has a regression that fails on pre-fix code; suite includes the F8 NaN open+work+fold sequence on a temp copy, bounds matrix, orphan both-skips, recover preserve-orphan, auto-open single- vs multi-worker, attempt-pair T-001/T-002/T-005 shapes, F10 catalog-namespace / makeFinding probe (new review.* without lint-catalog entry), and status open-vs-folded; bun run validate:ci and bun run ngrace lint --path . are green on this repository.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit and CLI regressions under src/grace-cursor.test.ts, src/grace-status.test.ts, src/review/core.test.ts, and src/lint/catalog.test.ts (F10 scanner repair) that fail before the fix and pass after; dogfooding ngrace lint --path . green; validate:ci green. TraceAssertion-backed verification for M-CURSOR, M-STATUS, M-REVIEW as needed; no new Marker evidence. Recover and bounds paths proven via command errors, not new src/lint/catalog.ts production codes. New attempt-pair code has a REVIEW_CATALOG entry (and exact guide or documented allowlist treatment only if required after the scanner sees it).

Assumptions.Assumption: p0-cursor-derivation.md (measured at 60c752f) plus D8.1–D8.8 are authoritative for this bundle's under-specifications; F8.2 corrects the :470-only and status-as-skip-consumer mis-cites. F10 / F10.2 amend the P0.10 emission path and the former "file-disjoint with C-TOKEN" premise.

Refuted and corrected (F10): the draft assumption that a new review.* finding code can be emitted without catalog-test work, and that review.* codes live solely under M-REVIEW with no interaction with src/lint/catalog.test.ts, is false at HEAD. Emitting review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated (object form or otherwise) fails catalog exact-guide completeness until the scanner routes review.* to REVIEW_CATALOG and sees makeFinding's positional codes. P0.10 therefore depends on AC-REVIEW-CATALOG-NAMESPACE; the new code is registered in REVIEW_CATALOG (src/review/catalog.ts), not src/lint/catalog.ts.

Finding-level clearance schema does not exist today. D8.6 accepts attaching the P0.10 finding to the gate verdict note keyed by findingId at warning severity, with the binding property that the reviewer's reason text is recorded. If implementation discovers that gate verdict notes cannot carry a stable findingId key or free-text reason, stop and report — inventing ledger schema is the authority's call, not the implementer's (D8.6).

Non-test path rule for P0.10 is path suffix .test.ts / .test.js only (aligned with review/core.ts:418). Paths under src/test-support/ are not treated as tests unless they use those suffixes. Plan/spec/docs in ObservedWriteScope are non-test; a docs-only fail→pass pair still raises the finding and needs a recorded reason.

WriteEvidence today digests git porcelain changed files; the attempt-pair check intersects those digests with the plan's ObservedWriteScope (same expansion family as the scope audit), not the full dirty tree alone.

C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY remains active and unarchived until this bundle lands and the authority separately authorizes recover --fix on that real ledger (rule 7; F8.1; F9). This bundle's tests never mutate that path. Per F10.2, sequential overlap on src/lint/catalog.test.ts is declared and justified; C-TOKEN's five tasks are complete so concurrent writes under that bundle are not expected.
Explicit --worker w0 remains indistinguishable from default w0 (D8.2 residual); multi-worker refuse uses distinct worker values, not "was the flag passed".

After makeFinding becomes visible to the scanner, some or all of the thirteen pre-existing review.* codes may lack exact REVIEW_CATALOG guides and will need a frozen allowlist entry (F10). The new attempt-pair code itself must have an exact REVIEW_CATALOG guide (not sit on that backlog allowlist), matching T-005's rule that newly-erroring codes are never allowlisted.
